input.hypothesis: Candidate_920 already satisfies every sampled bilateral displacement, recovery, progressive-stiffness, slack-to-taut, and no-contact bound, while its low and recovery windows remain dynamically unqualified. The local payout/routing interaction in result_19 showed only a small direction-specific payout effect and no recorded routing-radius effect at the tested scale. Redistributing 0.01 m of backbone length from the distal segment to the proximal segment, while preserving the total 0.30 m backbone length and all materials, sections, routing, and payouts, should reduce distal inertial leverage and increase proximal compliance contribution enough to reduce low-stage and recovery motion without eliminating direction-selective tendon engagement.
input.interpretation: This is joint design exploration. Because both lengths change simultaneously, any observed effect belongs to the length-redistribution block and is not attributed to either segment length alone. The next decision is to diagnose and dynamically evaluate the generated candidate if construction succeeds.
input.stopping_condition: Stop this design branch after one matched bilateral dynamic comparison of the generated candidate. Continue toward complete qualification only if task margins and mirrored recruitment remain intact and at least one low/recovery settling observable improves materially; otherwise revise span topology or damping distribution.
input.weakening_observation: If the redistribution materially reduces low-load displacement, loses progressive stiffening or mirrored tendon recruitment, creates route or contact problems, or leaves low/recovery motion unchanged or worse, then this proximal-distal length redistribution is not useful and the next decision should explore distributed-anchor span topology or a different nonuniform damping distribution rather than further payout/radius tuning.
